task_instance: Compact a simulated coding-session conversation (a git repo with a PRD, two commits, and dirty uncommitted work, plus a transcript containing accidental secrets/PII) into a 5-section handoff document, redact secrets before save, suggest 3-5 skills, and refresh the handoff in place for a follow-up goal.
evidence: Built sample_project/ (git repo, 2 commits: fbe0f94 docs PRD, 723ea05 feat add(); dirty tree with uncommitted app.py edit and an untracked .env containing a fake Stripe key + DB connection string) and conversation_transcript.md containing the same secrets plus the user's email and two undecided questions. Implemented handoff_template_generator.py (reads git log/status from the repo, fills the 5 required headers: 'Goal of next session', 'State of play', 'Open decisions', 'Skills to use', 'Artifacts', referencing PRD.md/commit hashes/repo path instead of pasting their contents) and redaction_linter.py (regex-based scan+redact for API keys, DB connection strings, JWTs, private-key blocks, dotenv secret lines, emails). Ran: `python3 handoff_template_generator.py --goal '...' --repo sample_project --transcript conversation_transcript.md --out fake_os_tmp/handoff-20260927.md` producing the draft, then `python3 redaction_linter.py fake_os_tmp/handoff-20260927.md --mode strict`, which found and redacted 4 items (stripe_key, generic_api_key, db_conn_string, email). Verified via grep that `sk_live_51H8`, `sup3rSecret`, and `example` no longer appear in the saved file (all three greps returned 0 matches) while the doc still has all 6 '## ' headers (5 required + 1 raw-notes section used only to prove the linter scanned real content). Also exercised the skill's '--refresh' behavior: reran the generator with --refresh and a new goal string against the same output path; confirmed the file was edited in place (not a new file) and only the Goal section changed. Note: per the sandbox's safety rules, output was written to a work-directory subfolder (fake_os_tmp/) standing in for the OS temp directory the skill would normally target (mktemp -t handoff-XXXXXX.md) or ~/.config/handoff — this is a path substitution only, not a functional gap; the underlying deliverable (generate+redact+save+refresh a 5-section handoff doc using only python3/git already installed) fully works offline with no missing tool.
